input.quote: (b) Contractor shall bill Company as set forth in the relevant Statement of Work. Each invoice submitted by Contractor will provide supporting detail for the Services invoiced, including, to the extent applicable to a particular engagement, the dates of Services and hours worked at the applicable rate by Statement of Work.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no audit, inspection or verification clause at all: searches for "audit", "inspect" and "verif" return no hits, and §3 addresses only Contractor's invoicing obligations to us, with no verification mechanic in either direction. Because the playbook expects an audit clause with express limits and none exists anywhere in the document, this is recorded as missing rather than compliant, and the deterministic frequency check cannot be satisfied without clause text. The redline is drafted defensively so that it concedes nothing: new §3(d) opens by confirming Contractor has no audit right, and then caps any verification right that a Statement of Work or applicable law might otherwise supply at the preferred position — once per twelve months, 30 days' prior written notice, normal business hours, an independent non-competitor auditor under a confidentiality agreement, off-site review only with no direct, remote or on-site access to our systems, and Contractor bearing all cost unless it establishes an underpayment over 5%. This keeps our current advantage while closing the SOW gap, and the comment offers the fallback (15 days' notice, 10% threshold) if RadialSpark pushes back.

proposal.summary: Insert §3(d) capping any Contractor verification/audit of Company: once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, Contractor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no access to Company systems.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement is silent on any Contractor right to audit or verify our records, so we have added §3(d) to confirm that limit expressly: any such verification is once per 12 months, on 30 days' notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor under confidentiality, at your cost unless an underpayment over 5% is found, and with no access to our systems. This is our standard audit position and simply preserves the status quo; we can move to 15 days' notice and a 10% threshold if helpful.

ops.text: (d) Contractor shall have no right to audit, inspect or verify Company's books, records, systems or usage except as expressly set forth in this Section 3(d). To the extent any Statement of Work or applicable law provides Contractor with any such audit, inspection or verification right, it shall be exercised no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Company, during Company's normal business hours, by an independent third-party auditor that is not a competitor of Company and that has executed a written confidentiality agreement reasonably acceptable to Company, and shall be conducted off-site through review of records Company provides, without any direct, remote or on-site access to Company's systems, networks or facilities. Contractor shall bear all costs of any such audit, inspection or verification unless it establishes an underpayment by Company exceeding five percent (5%) of amounts properly due for the period audited.
